evidence.title: Privileged access recertification is 11 months overdue
evidence.description: The last attestation of who holds administrative rights was completed before the previous CISO left. 340 accounts have not been reviewed since.
evidence.interpretation: Nobody can currently say who can administer Nexora.

evidence.title: MFA exception register holds 214 accounts
evidence.description: Most exceptions were granted as temporary. The oldest is three years old. Nineteen are administrative.
evidence.interpretation: Reported MFA coverage is materially better than actual coverage.

evidence.title: Provider engineers hold standing administrative accounts
evidence.description: Fourteen named accounts belonging to Corvus Managed Services carry permanent privileged rights in the identity platform. None expire.
evidence.interpretation: Nexora's most privileged users are not Nexora employees.

evidence.title: Provider access does not enforce second factor
evidence.description: Vendor remote access accepts password-only authentication for the managed service provider's engineers.
evidence.interpretation: The most privileged route into the estate is also the least protected.

evidence.title: Supplier assurance questionnaire returned clean
evidence.description: Corvus returned a fully compliant questionnaire, including a claim of enforced multi-factor authentication for all privileged access.
evidence.interpretation: Assurance paperwork contradicts the technical evidence. One of them is wrong.

evidence.title: Access review for order management failed
evidence.description: A sample review found nine leavers with active accounts and two accounts with rights nobody could explain.
evidence.interpretation: Identity lifecycle is not working, which makes every access decision unreliable.

evidence.title: Service account estate is unowned
evidence.description: 412 non-human accounts. 78 have passwords older than five years. 31 hold privileged rights.
evidence.interpretation: A large, invisible population of credentials with no owner and no rotation.

evidence.title: Privileged vault covers a third of administrators
evidence.description: The vault was deployed two years ago. Adoption stopped when the infrastructure team objected to session recording.
evidence.interpretation: The control exists. It does not cover the people who matter most.

evidence.title: Warehouse platform runs on unsupported software
evidence.description: The Meridian warehouse platform runs on an operating system that left vendor support 14 months ago. No patch path exists.
evidence.interpretation: A business-critical platform that cannot be patched, supporting despatch for three distribution centres.

evidence.title: Legacy data centre can route into production
evidence.description: A firewall review found permissive rules between the legacy estate and the production zone, added during the 2022 migration and never removed.
evidence.interpretation: The legacy estate is not isolated, so its weakness is the production zone's weakness.

evidence.title: Architecture documentation states legacy is isolated
evidence.description: The current architecture pack describes the legacy data centre as fully segregated from production.
evidence.interpretation: The documentation is two network changes out of date.

evidence.title: No current inventory of the legacy estate
evidence.description: Three separate asset lists disagree on how many systems remain in the legacy data centre. The range is 60 to 140.
evidence.interpretation: You cannot protect, patch or migrate what nobody has counted.

evidence.title: A restore, timed from the request
evidence.description: Engineering restored a critical service into a clean environment and timed it from the moment it was asked for, not from when the engineers started. The steps that needed somebody who knew the system are now written down.
evidence.interpretation: A recovery time you have measured is worth more than one you have been promised.

evidence.title: Last recovery test did not complete
evidence.description: The most recent restore test was abandoned after eleven hours. The report was never reissued.
evidence.interpretation: Recovery time objectives are aspirations, not measurements.

evidence.title: Backup platform shares administrative credentials with production
evidence.description: The backup platform is administered with the same privileged accounts as the systems it protects.
evidence.interpretation: An actor with production administration can destroy the recovery path at the same time.

evidence.title: Legacy systems are outside the backup schedule
evidence.description: A sample showed that 23 legacy systems, including two supporting despatch, are not covered by the central backup schedule.
evidence.interpretation: The systems least able to defend themselves are also the least recoverable.

evidence.title: Ransomware activity rising in the sector
evidence.description: Three comparable payment and logistics businesses have been extorted in the last quarter. Two were reached through managed service providers.
evidence.interpretation: The technique that is working elsewhere is available here.

evidence.title: Credential stuffing against sector partner portals
evidence.description: Threat intelligence reports a sustained campaign against extranet and partner portals in the sector.
evidence.interpretation: Nexora's partner portal is the kind of target currently being worked through systematically.

evidence.title: Sector data platforms targeted by a patient actor
evidence.description: An intelligence briefing describes an actor collecting behavioural data sets from analytics providers over long periods.
evidence.interpretation: The data lake is commercially interesting to someone willing to wait.

evidence.title: Exploit published for the checkout framework
evidence.description: A working exploit for the framework version used by the checkout service was published this week.
evidence.interpretation: An internet-facing weakness has just become cheap to use.

evidence.title: 6,283 critical vulnerabilities outstanding
evidence.description: The scanner reports 6,283 findings at critical severity across the estate.
evidence.interpretation: Volume, not risk. Severity ratings here describe the finding, not Nexora's exposure.

evidence.title: 1,900 critical findings on isolated development systems
evidence.description: A third of the critical findings sit on a development cluster with no inbound routes and no real data.
evidence.interpretation: Severe-looking findings on systems that do not matter. Fixing these would feel productive and change nothing.

evidence.title: Eleven exploitable findings on internet-facing services
evidence.description: Eleven findings are on services reachable from the internet, three of them with public exploit code.
evidence.interpretation: A small, material subset hidden inside a very large number.

evidence.title: Median time to remediate is 94 days
evidence.description: Critical findings on production systems take a median of 94 days to close.
evidence.interpretation: Remediation capacity, not detection capacity, is the constraint.

evidence.title: SOC receives no telemetry from the legacy estate
evidence.description: The SOC's log source inventory shows nothing from the legacy data centre and only partial cloud control-plane coverage.
evidence.interpretation: Detection coverage claims are about the tools, not the estate.

evidence.title: SOC escalation quality is poor
evidence.description: Of 340 escalations last quarter, 318 were false positives. The team has started closing them without reading.
evidence.interpretation: Alert fatigue is itself a control failure: the real one will look like the others.

evidence.title: Unexplained out-of-hours access through vendor remote access
evidence.description: A low-confidence anomaly: vendor remote access sessions at 03:40 on three consecutive nights, outside the provider's contracted hours.
evidence.interpretation: Could be provider maintenance. Could be someone else using provider credentials.

evidence.title: Recurring alerts from network printers
evidence.description: A cluster of high-severity alerts turns out to be a misconfigured print server scanning the network nightly.
evidence.interpretation: Benign. Worth fixing, not worth a programme.

evidence.title: Publicly readable storage in the production tenancy
evidence.description: Two storage buckets in production permit anonymous read. One contains application logs including session identifiers.
evidence.interpretation: A small misconfiguration with a direct path to customer impact.

evidence.title: Non-production is peered to production
evidence.description: A network peering link between the development and production tenancies was created for a migration in 2023 and never removed.
evidence.interpretation: The weakest environment has a route into the strongest.

evidence.title: Deployment pipeline holds standing production credentials
evidence.description: The build pipeline authenticates to production with a long-lived credential shared across 40 repositories.
evidence.interpretation: Anyone who can influence a build can reach production.

evidence.title: Container workloads run with excessive permissions
evidence.description: Workloads on the shared cluster inherit a role permitting broad read access to production data stores.
evidence.interpretation: A compromise of any workload becomes a compromise of customer data.

evidence.title: Behavioural data lake has 190 standing readers
evidence.description: 190 accounts hold read access to the behavioural data lake, including 40 who have changed role since it was granted.
evidence.interpretation: The commercial crown jewels are readable by a population nobody manages.

evidence.title: Customer data retained beyond policy
evidence.description: Records for closed accounts are retained indefinitely in the analytics estate, contrary to the published retention policy.
evidence.interpretation: Data that should not exist cannot be breached, and this data exists.

evidence.title: Cardholder data appears outside the payment environment
evidence.description: A discovery scan found unencrypted card data in two application log stores outside the defined payment environment.
evidence.interpretation: The regulated boundary is wider than anyone has been told.

evidence.title: Partner portal accounts share the staff directory
evidence.description: Partner identities are held in the same identity platform, and the same tenant, as employee accounts.
evidence.interpretation: A partner credential compromise starts from inside the staff identity boundary.

evidence.title: Logistics integration account has write access
evidence.description: The integration account used by Lattice Logistics can write to and delete records in order management, not simply read them.
evidence.interpretation: The integration has far more authority than the integration needs.

evidence.title: HR provider reports a security incident
evidence.description: People Cloud has notified customers of unauthorised access to a support system. Nexora's exposure is unconfirmed.
evidence.interpretation: Possibly nothing. Possibly employee data. Somebody has to find out.

evidence.title: Incident response plan has never been exercised
evidence.description: The plan names an incident commander who left the business in March. No exercise has been run in two years.
evidence.interpretation: The first time the plan is used will be the first time it is tested.

evidence.title: No incident response retainer in place
evidence.description: There is no contracted external response capability. The previous retainer lapsed at renewal.
evidence.interpretation: External help would have to be procured during the incident, at the worst possible moment.

evidence.title: Five security vacancies, two over six months old
evidence.description: The security teams are carrying five unfilled roles. The two in identity engineering have been open since before the previous CISO left.
evidence.interpretation: Capacity, not strategy, will be the constraint on everything this year.

evidence.title: A security lead flags sustained overload
evidence.description: One of your heads of function reports their team has been running above sustainable load since the last major project.
evidence.interpretation: Delegating more will produce less, not more.

evidence.title: Undocumented integration found between analytics and the CRM
evidence.description: An engineer mentions in passing that analytics pulls directly from the CRM through a service account created for a 2021 project.
evidence.interpretation: The architecture diagram is a subset of the architecture.

evidence.title: External audit repeats last year's privileged access finding
evidence.description: The external auditors have raised privileged access management for the third consecutive year.
evidence.interpretation: The board has been told about this before. They will remember.

evidence.title: Risk register entries have not moved in 18 months
evidence.description: Of 23 open entries, 19 have no update, owner activity or review since the previous CISO's first quarter.
evidence.interpretation: The register records what was once worried about, not what is currently true.

evidence.title: Penetration test reached production from a corporate laptop
evidence.description: The annual test moved from a standard corporate device to production administrative access in under two days.
evidence.interpretation: The path is not theoretical; it has been walked.

evidence.title: Penetration test scope excluded the legacy estate
evidence.description: The test scope was agreed as cloud and corporate only. The legacy data centre was excluded on cost grounds.
evidence.interpretation: The clean result covers the part of the estate least likely to fail.

evidence.title: Acquisition target's security posture is undocumented
evidence.description: Due diligence on Kestrel Digital covered financials thoroughly. The technology review was a single questionnaire.
evidence.interpretation: Nexora is about to connect an estate it has never examined to its own network.

evidence.title: Platform launch date is fixed and public
evidence.description: The launch has been announced to the market. The delivery team is working to a date that cannot move without a commercial cost.
evidence.interpretation: Any security condition on the launch is a negotiation, not an instruction.

evidence.title: Warehouse systems wiped at two logistics firms
evidence.description: A group calling itself Black Tern has wiped warehouse systems at two logistics firms in the region. There was no ransom note. Both came in through remote access appliances a version or two behind.
evidence.interpretation: Somebody is attacking businesses like this one for the outage, not the money.

evidence.title: The remote access appliance is two versions behind
evidence.description: The upgrade needs a weekend outage, and every request for one has been turned down since the spring.
evidence.interpretation: The front door of the network has known flaws in it.

evidence.title: A supplier's bank details were changed on an email
evidence.description: Accounts payable changed a supplier's bank details on the strength of an email from the supplier's real address, and caught it only when the supplier chased payment.
evidence.interpretation: An email is all it takes to redirect a payment.

evidence.title: A forwarding rule on a finance mailbox
evidence.description: A finance mailbox forwards anything with 'invoice' in the subject to an outside address. Nobody in finance set it up.
evidence.interpretation: Somebody may already be reading finance's mail.

evidence.title: The pipeline deploys whatever it is given
evidence.description: Nothing in the build pipeline checks who wrote a change or whether it was reviewed before it reaches customers.
evidence.interpretation: Whoever reaches the pipeline reaches every customer.
